title: HiddenMixedIntegerLinear.lean

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Bounded mixed-integer linear optimization: minimize cᵀz+dᵀy subject to Az+Gy≤b, z∈ℤᵖ, lo≤z≤hi, and y∈ℝᑫ. The objective is linear; integrality makes the feasible domain generally nonconvex.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact box-restricted LP optimization oracle. A query supplies integer lower and upper bounds; the reply is an optimal continuous relaxation point or none certifying infeasibility. Correctness holds for every history and seed; arbitrary optimal-point selection is permitted. Each complete LP query counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HiddenMixedIntegerLinear.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.lean: IsRelaxationOracle, SolvesRelaxation, RelaxationFeasible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Integer variables lie in ℤᵖ and continuous variables in ℝᑫ, with finitely many linear inequalities. Integer coordinates have public finite bounds; continuous coordinates need not be bounded.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Only p, q, c, d, lo, hi are public. The constraint count m, matrices A and G, right-hand side b, and certificate λ are hidden. Validity requires either λ≥0 and d+λᵀG=0, or infeasibility of the initial continuous relaxation. The extracted budget depends on the hidden cardinality of goodPoints, whose Lagrangian values are lower bounds on every mixed-feasible objective value.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HiddenMixedIntegerLinear.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, lagrangian, goodPoints; supplied OracleTemplate.HiddenMixedIntegerLinear.result budget.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Exact global optimality: a returned solution must be mixed-feasible and have objective no larger than every mixed-feasible solution. No positive epsilon tolerance is present.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: Return an exact feasible optimizer, or none only when no mixed-feasible solution exists.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: Success is required for every outcome ω, including every algorithm and oracle seed, rather than merely in expectation or almost surely.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The underlying optimization problem is standard MILP, but hidden constraints accessed exclusively through an exact box-relaxation oracle, together with a hidden-certificate-dependent call budget, create an unusual information and complexity model.

descriptionHtml:
Hidden Mixed-Integer Linear Optimization

We consider linear optimization over Zp×Rq, where p,q are nonnegative integers, with known objective coefficients and finite integer bounds but hidden linear inequality constraints. Either the continuous relaxation is infeasible, or hidden nonnegative constraint multipliers cancel the continuous-variable coefficients in the Lagrangian. Given an integer box, the oracle returns an exact optimizer of the continuous relaxation restricted to that box and the original bounds, or reports infeasibility. The goal is to return an exact mixed-integer global optimizer, or correctly report infeasibility, for every realization of any algorithm and oracle randomness.

Write the objective as f(z,y)=c⊤z+d⊤y, where c∈Rp and d∈Rq. The problem is min(z,y)∈Ff(z,y),F={(z,y)∈Zp×Rq:Az+Gy≤b, ℓ≤z≤u}. Here m≥0 is an integer, A∈Rm×p, G∈Rm×q, b∈Rm, and ℓ,u∈Zp. All vector inequalities are componentwise. The algorithm receives only p,q,c,d,ℓ,u; the hidden data m,A,G,b and multiplier vector λ∈Rm may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

For any query box β=(a,h)∈Zp×Zp, define Rβ={(z,y)∈Rp×Rq:Az+Gy≤b, ℓ≤z≤u, a≤z≤h}. In particular, R(ℓ,u) is the full continuous relaxation. Query endpoints need not lie within the original bounds or be ordered; the intersection above determines feasibility.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Hidden multiplier certificate). The hidden parameters satisfy the disjunction (λ≥0  and  d+G⊤λ=0)orR(ℓ,u)=∅.

Assumption 2 (Exact relaxation oracle). For every query box β, the oracle reports infeasibility exactly when Rβ=∅. Otherwise it returns a point (zβ,yβ) satisfying (zβ,yβ)∈Rβ,f(zβ,yβ)≤f(z,y)for every (z,y)∈Rβ. These requirements hold for every query history and every realization of oracle randomness; the choice among optimizers may depend on both. Algorithm randomness is independent of oracle randomness.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output is either an infeasibility report or a pair (z¯,y¯)∈Zp×Rq. An infeasibility report must satisfy F=∅; a returned pair must satisfy (z¯,y¯)∈F,f(z¯,y¯)≤f(z,y)for every (z,y)∈F. The corresponding requirement must hold for every realization of algorithm and oracle randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Minimize c⊤z+d⊤y subject to Az+Gy≤b, ℓ≤z≤u, z∈Zp, y∈Rq, with real data and integer bounds. Only p,q,c,d,ℓ,u are public. Either the root LP is infeasible or a hidden λ≥0 satisfies d+G⊤λ=0. Each box-LP call returns an exact optimizer or reports infeasibility, with arbitrary optimal-solution choices. The target is an exact mixed-integer optimum or a correct infeasibility report for every execution.

Exact hidden mixed-integer linear optimization: HiddenMixedIntegerLinear.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) BestBoundHiddenMilp (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O(min{N,1+p|Gλ|}) box-LP calls
(2) Best-bound B&B (Dey et al. 2021, Theorem 3) O(1+p|Gλ∗|) LP calls. Special case: pure binary IP, q=0, [ℓ,u]=[0,1]p; optimal root dual λ∗. (1): Scope extends to bounded integers and continuous variables, with range-free factor p and any feasible λ. Matches the binary rate at λ=λ∗. (1): Good-point term has twice the leading constant on the binary overlap.
(3) Classical finite-tree bound (LongTails, n.d.) O(N) box-LP calls (full setup; bounded-below root LP). (1): Gap-dependent saving when p|Gλ|=o(N); retains the finite-tree cap. Hidden constraints suffice.
(4) Enumeration, derived bound (LongTails, n.d.) O(N) box-LP calls, one degenerate box per integer point (full setup). (1): Fewer calls if 1+4p|Gλ|<N. Binary example: |Gλ|≤p3 gives O(p4) versus O(2p); at p=60, about 5⋅107 versus 260. (1): Up to twice the call bound when |Gλ|≈N.

Abbr: LP: linear program; IP: integer program; B&B: branch-and-bound. N=∏j=1pmax{uj−ℓj+1,0}; OPT is the mixed-integer optimal value, with OPT=+∞ for infeasibility; Gλ={z∈Zp∩[ℓ,u]:(c+A⊤λ)⊤z−λ⊤b≤OPT}. λ∗ denotes an optimal root-LP dual multiplier. Costs count LP solves, not arithmetic operations.

Dey, Santanu S., Yatharth Dubey, and Marco Molinaro. 2021. Branch-and-Bound Solves Random Binary IPs in Polytime. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2007.15192.

import LongTails.Setups.BoundedMixedIntegerLinear
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi
import Mathlib.Order.Interval.Finset.Defs

namespace LongTails.Setups.HiddenMixedIntegerLinear

open OracleTemplate Matrix

structure Public where
  p : ℕ
  q : ℕ
  c : Fin p → ℝ
  d : Fin q → ℝ
  lo : Fin p → ℤ
  hi : Fin p → ℤ

structure Params extends Public where
  m : ℕ
  A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin p) ℝ
  G : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin q) ℝ
  b : Fin m → ℝ
  lam : Fin m → ℝ

abbrev data (P : Params) : BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.Params :=
  ⟨P.p, P.q, P.m, P.A, P.G, P.b, P.c, P.d, P.lo, P.hi⟩

abbrev Box (Q : Public) := (Fin Q.p → ℤ) × (Fin Q.p → ℤ)

abbrev Point (Q : Public) := (Fin Q.p → ℝ) × (Fin Q.q → ℝ)

abbrev Solution (Q : Public) := (Fin Q.p → ℤ) × (Fin Q.q → ℝ)

def lagrangian (P : Params) (z : Fin P.p → ℝ) : ℝ := (P.c + P.lam ᵥ* P.A) ⬝ᵥ z - P.lam ⬝ᵥ P.b

noncomputable def goodPoints (P : Params) : Finset (Fin P.p → ℤ) :=
  open Classical in
  (Fintype.piFinset fun j => Finset.Icc (P.lo j) (P.hi j)).filter fun z =>
    ∀ x, BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.MixedFeasible (data P) x →
      lagrangian P (fun j => (z j : ℝ)) ≤
        BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.objective (data P) (BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.toPoint (data P) x)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance _ := Unit
  Query Q := Box Q
  Reply Q := Option (Point Q)
  Output Q := Option (Solution Q)
  publicInput P := P.toPublic
  valid P := ((∀ i, 0 ≤ P.lam i) ∧ P.d + P.lam ᵥ* P.G = 0) ∨
    ∀ x, ¬ BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.RelaxationFeasible (data P) (P.lo, P.hi) x
  admissible P _ O := BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.IsRelaxationOracle (data P) O
  successful P _ output _ := ∀ ω, BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.SolvesMixed (data P) (output ω)

end LongTails.Setups.HiddenMixedIntegerLinear
